clue.text: Element discovered by an Athenian: yttrium

parts.note: taken as written
Timon of Athens, the misanthrope of Shakespeare's play, is a famous Athenian
Y is the chemical symbol for yttrium

explanation.surface: A chemistry history note: some element was found by a Greek scientist, and it was yttrium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Athenian' suggests an ancient Greek scientist, but it points to one particular Athenian, Shakespeare's Timon.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a metalloid chemical element, symbol Sb.

clue.text: Gold fruit, new variety of android

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: A golden fruit, a new type of robot.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a self-operating machine, a kind of robot like an android.

clue.text: To make the effort takes time and money

parts.note: the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: A remark that making the effort costs both time and money.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble, as in 'don't trouble to reply', means to take pains or make the effort.

clue.text: Complaint from blue-stocking?

explanation.surface: A grievance raised by a bookish woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A blue-stocking is an intellectual woman, so fancifully a lady with an MA degree: MA LADY. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an illness, which is also called a complaint.

clue.text: Shamingly identify initiator of crude expletive to get some publicity

parts.note: to name someone, as in 'name and shame', is to identify them publicly to shame them

indicators.note: the initiator of a word is its first letter, here of crude

parts.note: heck is a mild exclamation of annoyance

explanation.surface: Outing someone who started swearing crudely, for the sake of publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A namecheck is a public mention of someone, which gives them a little publicity.

clue.text: Southern scoundrel, very heartless and despicable

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel

indicators.note: with its heart gone, the word very keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A description of a low villain from the South: thoroughly heartless and contemptible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle ER of 'very', leaving VY.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurvy as an adjective is an old word for mean, contemptible or worthless.

clue.text: Dog that's trailing explorer

indicators.note: the second piece follows behind the first, as something trails after

parts.note: Robert Falcon Scott was the British Antarctic explorer
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dog following behind an explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog that's' reads as 'the dog that is', but 'that's' gives the letters of the Latin abbreviation id est.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottie is a Scottish terrier, a breed of dog.

clue.text: Comprehensive cooking ruins veal

indicators.note: cooking works the ingredients into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thorough verdict: bad cooking spoils the veal.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means applying to everything, which is comprehensive.

clue.text: Check king with a knight that may have done a lot of attacking

definitions.text: that may have done a lot of attacking

parts.note: to vet is to check or screen
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A chess move: putting the king in check with a knight, by an aggressive player.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture of check, king and knight misleads; each word gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is an old soldier who has seen much fighting.

clue.text: Brace and bit used by competent woman

indicators.note: a bit of the words competent woman is used, so the letters sit across those two words

explanation.surface: A carpenter's brace and bit, wielded by a capable woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brace and bit' reads as the drilling tool, but 'Brace' alone is the definition and 'bit used by' points to compeTENT WOman.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace of pheasants or pistols is a pair, so a brace means a couple.

clue.text: Author of attack on mail — post has gone astray

indicators.note: something that has gone astray has wandered out of place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a letter has been lost in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ON MAIL and POST are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a satirical attack, and one who writes lampoons is their author.

clue.text: Whale's body cut up and fed to dog (The Miller)

definitions.note: read as 'whale is', the definition is the whale of the novel

indicators.note: the dog's name takes the other letters into itself, as food is fed to it

parts.note: Mick the Miller was a famous British greyhound of the 1920s and 30s

indicators.note: something cut up is in pieces, so the letters of body are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: a whale carcass chopped and given to a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Mick the Miller was a champion British greyhound; the brackets around 'The Miller' make it look like a separate aside, but it completes the dog's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The white whale of Herman Melville's novel bears this name.

clue.text: Other people have accepted an alternative hypothesis.

indicators.note: the first piece takes the second inside it, as one accepts something into a group

parts.note: they is the pronoun for other people
or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Others have come round to a different explanation.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed explanation, a synonym of hypothesis.

clue.text: … in another case, they get marks for second half of it

definitions.note: the pronoun they in the objective case rather than the nominative

indicators.note: the second half of that six-letter word, its last three letters, is the part removed

parts.note: after the ellipsis, it refers back to the previous answer in the clue before
M is an abbreviation for marks, the German currency

explanation.surface: Following on, a grading rule: in another case the students get marks for the second half.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 11 Across, so 'it' is that answer; 'for' says M replaces its second half, ORY, leaving THE + M.
explanation.definitionFit: The objective case of the pronoun they is the form used after verbs and prepositions.

clue.text: Historic vessel takes weeks to sink after outbreak of fire

parts.note: May is a month, a span of weeks

indicators.note: the outbreak of something is its start, so the first letter of fire

parts.note: to sink is to lower

explanation.surface: An old ship takes a long time to go down after a fire breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking 'weeks' as the month of May is loose, but it is the only reading that fits. 'takes' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620.

clue.text: Haven't seen change occurring at a very favourable time

definitions.text: occurring at a very favourable time

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the letters of the words before it into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remarks they haven't noticed any change.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heaven-sent arrives providentially, at exactly the right moment.

clue.text: Having suppressed resistance, disappeared —- that's glossed over

indicators.note: the second word holds the letter down inside itself

parts.note: to have vanished is to have disappeared
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An official cover-up: resistance crushed, people gone, all whitewashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnished can mean given a deceptively attractive gloss, a figurative glossing over.

clue.text: Casual blow

explanation.surface: A light, offhand punch.
explanation.walkthrough: As an adjective it means offhand, as in a throwaway remark; as a verb phrase it means squander, as in to blow money.
explanation.definitionFit: A throwaway remark is casual, and to throw away money is to blow it.

clue.text: Magazine's written for Yankees

explanation.surface: A note that a periodical's article was aimed at Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written for' is a link: the first reading is the New Yorker magazine with its possessive, the second the people of New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Yorker is a magazine, and Yankees is a name for natives of New York.

clue.text: Pain each club inflicted on man

indicators.note: the pieces are laid on top of the last one, which comes after them

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Every club brings hurt on a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' hints at a weapon, but it is the RAC, Britain's Royal Automobile Club.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is a pain in the ear.

clue.text: Salvage works miracle

indicators.note: works as a verb means operates on, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Rescuing something performs a miracle.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim is to recover something, which is to salvage it.

clue.text: Retreat, getting some foreign currency back

indicators.note: back says the word is read from right to left

parts.note: the rial is the currency of Iran and of Oman

explanation.surface: Withdrawing from a market as some overseas money returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RIAL into LAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a den or hideaway, a place of retreat.

clue.text: A drink upset, knocked over like this — it's Fate!

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: knocked over turns the word upside down, so it is read backwards

parts.note: so means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A drink spilt and knocked flying: fate at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PORT into TROP and 'knocked over' turns SO into OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropos is one of the three Fates of Greek myth, who cuts the thread of life.

clue.text: Loan shark certain to be found in ancient city

indicators.note: the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A moneylender is sure to turn up in an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at extortionate interest, as a loan shark does.

clue.text: Frisk prisoner finally that's into type of acid

indicators.note: the letter goes into the middle of the acid's name

parts.note: folic acid is one of the B vitamins

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word prisoner

explanation.surface: Searching an inmate and finding he is into some kind of drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisk' suggests a body search, but as the definition it means to romp.
explanation.definitionFit: To frisk is to skip about playfully, which is to frolic.

clue.text: Flight attendants have adopted singular means of propulsion

indicators.note: the crew takes the letter in among its own, as a family adopts a child

parts.note: an aircrew is the staff who attend to an aircraft in flight
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Cabin crew have taken up an odd way of getting about.
explanation.definitionFit: An airscrew is an aircraft propeller, which drives it forward.

clue.text: Lasso attached to front of Chattanooga choo-choo?

definitions.text: attached to front of Chattanooga choo-choo?

explanation.surface: A rope lariat tied on the nose of the train from the old swing song.
explanation.walkthrough: A lasso catches cattle, so it is fancifully a cow catcher; the real cowcatcher is the frame at the front of American locomotives. 'Chattanooga Choo Choo' is a 1941 Glenn Miller song about a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is used to rope cattle, and a locomotive's front grid clears cattle from the track.

clue.text: Father's given wife a hand

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A father has offered his wife some help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hand' looks like help being given, but 'hand' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Paw is informal for a person's hand.

clue.text: You'd make a killing if you backed this horse

definitions.text: You'd make a killing if you backed this horse

parts.words: You'd make a killing if you backed this horse
parts.note: backing a horse means betting on it, but here backed means spelt backwards: the famous racehorse's name reversed gives a word for a killing

explanation.surface: A tipster's promise of a big win on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum was a racehorse that won Britain's Grand National three times in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Grand National winner's name read backwards is a word for murder.

clue.text: Raised wrongly? Yes, probably

indicators.note: letters put wrongly are out of their right order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: ay is an old and dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a thing was brought up wrongly and is told yes, most likely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' turns RAISED into IDARES.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild admission that something is likely, as 'probably' is.
